voyage.name: The Cross-Culture Warsaw Festival
voyage.content: World music festival. Concerts and music workshops, documentary screenings, exhibitions.

voyage.name: Jewish Culture Festival – The Singer's Warsaw
voyage.content: August.

voyage.name: Warsaw Film Festival
voyage.content: October.

voyage.name: Planete+ Doc Film Festival
voyage.content: Documentary films. May.

voyage.name: Burn Selector Festival
voyage.content: Electronic & alternative music festival. September.

voyage.name: Orange Warsaw Festival
voyage.content: Big pop music festival on the Horse Racetrack Służewiec. May.

voyage.name: Warsaw Summer Jazz Days
voyage.content: July.

voyage.name: Warsaw Autumn
voyage.content: International festival of contemporary music. September.

voyage.name: Long Night of Museums
voyage.content: A great opportunity to wander around with your date or friends and grab an ice cream cone from one of the many cafes that stay open late. Most museums and galleries will stay open past midnight. Noc Muzeów usually occurs around mid-May.

voyage.name: Atelier Amaro
voyage.content: Author's cuisine restaurant of chef Wojciech Modest Amaro. The restaurant does not offer à la carte dishes, in fact it doesn't have a fixed menu at all. Smart casual dress code is expected.

voyage.name: Senses
voyage.content: A "private dining" restaurant, author's cuisine of chef Andrea Camastra. Reservation required.

voyage.name: Targ Śniadaniowy
voyage.address: al. Wojska Polskiego 1; Skwer Grupy AK Granat and other places
voyage.content: Organised every weekend in various parts of town, usually

voyage.name: Monument to the Polish People Murdered in the East
voyage.content: "East" means "in the Soviet Union".

voyage.name: St. John's Cathedral
voyage.content: The Warsaw's cathedral was an opulent neo-Gothic church before World War II, but following its destruction it was rebuilt in a sombre, Masovian Gothic style resembling what is presumed to be its original form.

voyage.name: Jesuit Church
voyage.content: From the outside it seems like a large church, but step over the threshold and you'll see a rather modest and relatively small worship hall.

voyage.name: Kościół Bonifratrów Św. Jana Bożego
voyage.alt: St John of God Hospitallers Church

voyage.name: Galeria Obok ZPAF
voyage.hours: open only on events, call art gallery

voyage.name: Freta 33
voyage.content: Partly Italian.

voyage.name: Podwale 25 Kompania Piwna
voyage.content: Located on the border between the Old and New Town, this pub serves king-size portions of traditional Polish fare. Meals are accompanied by a free dish of pickled cucumbers and sauerkraut, while the bill comes with a shot of Polish cherry liquor. Beer is more average and solely pilsner, but it is drinkable and quite cheap. Free Wi-Fi connection. A bit noisy, but this is how a good pub should be.

voyage.name: Pasieka
voyage.content: Polish mead.

voyage.name: Hotel Le Regina Warsaw
voyage.content: Very comfortable hotel, that wants to go out of its way to make its guests comfortable. The hotel is located in the Old Town, but can be a little confusing to find, so be sure to take a cab or have the front desk to arrange for you to be picked up.

voyage.name: Palace of Culture and Science
voyage.price: Admission to the observation deck: 30 zł/25 zł (reduced)
voyage.content: Warsaw's most recognizable landmark has a controversial history: it was constructed in the 1950s ostensibly as a "gift" from the Soviet dictator Joseph Stalin. The gargantuan building is home to various institutions, including three theatres, a multiplex cinema, the Museum of Technology and the Congress Hall (built for Communist Party congresses, but mostly used for entertainment purposes now). An observation deck in

voyage.name: Tomb of The Unknown Soldier
voyage.content: Built in 1925, the tomb holds the remains of a Polish soldier who died in battle at Lwów, now Lviv, Ukraine. It also holds soil from 38 battlegrounds fought at by Poles.

voyage.name: Zamek Ujazdowski
voyage.content: The castle in Ujazdów became a secondary royal residence, and today hosts the contemporary art museum (see below).

voyage.name: Saxon Palace
voyage.content: The Saxon Kings of Poland have afforded themselves an imposing baroque palace, but sadly it was completely destroyed during Second World War. The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is the only remaining piece of the palace. Discussions are ongoing if the palace is to be rebuilt.

voyage.name: Palace on the Isle
voyage.content: Poland's last king, Stanisław August Poniatowski, preferred the relaxed and artsy atmosphere of the Łazienki Park and built himself a secondary residence there to meet with the contemporary statesmen, thinkers and artists.

voyage.name: Sejm Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej
voyage.content: Sejm is the name for the lower chamber of the Polish parliament, which since the 1930s meets in a peculiar circus-shaped building. The upper chamber, named Senat, occupies a rectangular building behind it. They are surrounded by a nice park.

voyage.name: Pałac Prezydencki
voyage.content: The impressive palace a few steps from the historic Old Town has served many functions in its long history, but now houses the offices of the President of Poland

voyage.name: Kancelaria Prezesa Rady Ministrów
voyage.content: The offices of the Prime Minister are the hub of the administrative branch of the government. Most important ministries are also housed in the immediate vicinity

voyage.name: Metropolitan
voyage.content: Designed by Sir Norman Foster and erected in 2003, the Metropolitan office building blends in with the surrounding historic buildings while standing out as an architectural masterpiece. The fountain in the freely accessible courtyard remains a photo favourite with tourists and locals.

voyage.name: Warsaw University Library
voyage.content: Built in 1999, the new home of the Warsaw University Library is a postmodernist building blending raw concrete with patinated copper. The building also features freely accessible extensive rooftop gardens providing interesting views over Warsaw. The building housing the Linguistics Faculty of the university opposite the library is also an interesting piece of modern architecture.

voyage.name: Eastern Wall
voyage.content: The "Eastern Wall" is a complex of buildings designed to flank the eastern side of the Palace of Culture and form a buffer between it and the rebuilt historic part further east. There are three highrise residential towers, a string of department stores and a restored pedestrian passage with a number of retail and gastronomic outlets. A part of Warsaw where the grey communist past meets the bustling colourful present

voyage.name: Rotunda
voyage.content: The round building was erected to house a bank branch, which it still does, but quickly became much more than that due to its very central location and large expanse of pavement around it, which makes it a favourite meeting spot for locals. The striking 1960s building suffered a tragedy in 1979, when a gas main exploded right below it, killing 49 people. This event is still remembered in Warsaw, making the rebuilt Ro

voyage.name: vitkAc
voyage.content: The luxury department store caused a huge stir when its facade clad in black stone debuted to the chagrin of inhabitants of a neighbouring residential building.

voyage.name: Nożyk Synagogue
voyage.content: Warsaw's only Orthodox Jewish synagogue in operation.

voyage.name: Umschlagplatz
voyage.content: The Umschlagplatz was the location Nazi officials herded Jews into cattle cars to be murdered at the Treblinka extermination camp. Estimates place the total number of persons transported from the Umschlagplatz at 300,000 or more.

voyage.name: POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews
voyage.content: New building opened in April 2013 awaits permanent exhibition.

voyage.name: Centrum Sztuki Współczesnej
voyage.content: An influential and popular exhibition space for contemporary art in the historic Zamek Ujazdowski, a former royal residence picturesquely situated on the escarpment between Park Ujazdowski and Łazienki Park.

voyage.name: Zachęta Gallery
voyage.content: A cool little gallery that mixes graffiti, sculptures, experimental painting, and photography.

voyage.name: National Museum
voyage.price: Free entry to permanent exhibitions on Tuesdays
voyage.content: The museum (really an art gallery) has a wonderful collection of paintings, sculptures, and depictions of the passion of the Christ. It houses several of Poland's most known paintings. Jan Matejko's Stańczyk painting depicts a famous jester to the Polish royalty in despair after Lithuania lost the city of Smolensk to Russia in 1514. The highlight is a gallery devoted to 1961–1964 excavations from Faras (previously Pa

voyage.name: Fotoplastikon
voyage.content: Established 1905, it is an IMAX one hundred years ago; a collection of unique 3D stereoscopic images from the 19th and 20th centuries.

voyage.name: Frederic Chopin Museum
voyage.content: Displays in English and Polish. The museum's design favours interactivity at the expense of information. Concerts on weekends.

voyage.name: Muzeum Techniki
voyage.content: A bit of a meta-museum, because it did not quite keep in with the times and became a fossizilied monument to old-style museums where you are not expected to experience or touch anything and just read the descriptions on the boards. That said, their collections of artifacts of all kinds of technologies are impressive, ranging from planes and cars to fully-functional scale models of steel mills and coal mines. Plus the

voyage.name: Chopin Family Living Room
voyage.hours: Summer (16 April-15 October): Tue-Sun 09:00-17:30. Winter: Tue-Sun 09:00-16:00. Closed Mondays, Easter Sat, the first day of the Easter holidays, 1 November, 24–26 December, and New Year's Day

voyage.name: Muzeum Ziemi PAN (Earth Museum, Polish Academy of Sciences)
Ethnographic Museum
voyage.price: Normal tickets cost 10 zł or 5 zł with a discount
voyage.content: Exhibitions that tell the stories of various societies and cultures. The bank building it is housed in is an interesting piece of 19th-century architecture.

voyage.name: Copernicus Science Centre
voyage.price: Entry 25 zł, reduced 16 zł (under 19s, over 65s students and disabled visitors), family tickets 66 zł (max 2 adults with 2 children), planetarium tickets starting at PLN 13
voyage.hours: Opening hours change throughout the year, check webpage for current hours. The Centre is always closed on Mondays
voyage.content: An exploration centre that brings together various branches of science and demonstrates their key principles and modern advances via interactive exhibits and experiments. There is plenty to interact with for visitors of all ages, although the centre was designed mainly with families with children in mind. There is also a planetarium, requiring a separate ticket

voyage.name: Ogród Saski
voyage.content: Ogród Saski is a lovely park in central Warsaw. It's small in comparison to Łazienki, but nonetheless relaxing with its forested landscape. Prior to World War II, it housed the Saxon Palace, which like the rest of Warsaw was destroyed in the insane Nazi vengeance for the Warsaw Uprising. Plans to rebuild the palace have failed to materialize due to funding. One of the draws aside from the escape of the city is the To

voyage.name: Łazienki Park
voyage.content: Łazienki Park was built and designed for a Polish politician, but became King Stanisław Poniatowski's, the last king of Poland, residence for much of later half of the 18th century. During Poniatowski's reign, many of the buildings on the park grounds were built. The most interesting buildings are the Łazienki Palace, Roman theater, and the so called Little White House, where the King sought the worldly comfort of mi

voyage.name: Ujazdów Park
voyage.content: Ujazdów Park, another beautiful park, lies just north of Łazienki, but is far less known and visited by tourists. One of the big draws to the park is the Ujazdów Castle, which dates its origins back to the 13th century. Over the centuries, the castles has housed princes, politicians, queens, kings, soldiers, and its current resident - the Center for Contemporary Art.

voyage.name: Ulica Kubusia Puchatka
voyage.content: A nondescript street in central Warsaw, whose claim to fame is that it's named after the children's book character Winnie the Pooh.

voyage.name: Greetings from Jerusalem Avenue
voyage.content: An artistic installation of an artificial palm tree (made of plastic and preserved imported palm tree leaves, periodically replaced), it was inspired by the artist's visit to Israel and the fact that Aleje Jerozolimskie, where it is placed, is named after New Jerusalem, a large pre-war Jewish settlement in Warsaw that does not exist anymore. It started as a very controversial landmark on one of the city's busiest rou

voyage.name: Koncerty Chopinowskie
voyage.content: Chopin concerts in Łazienki park, every Sunday at 12:00 and 16:00, from May to September.

voyage.name: Bajka
voyage.content: For children.

voyage.name: Polonia
voyage.content: Every production of this theatre founded by Polish stage and screen legend Krystyna Janda meets with huge publicity and has a long run.

voyage.name: Teatr Polski
voyage.content: A legendary institution showing mostly Polish and international classics. Many great names of Polish theatre have been calling this theatre home.

voyage.name: Prochoffnia
voyage.content: Unorthodox.

voyage.name: Roma
voyage.content: A musical theatre showing Polish versions of internationally acclaimed shows.

voyage.name: Studio Buffo
voyage.content: Unrelated to the one above.

voyage.name: TR (Rozmaitości)
voyage.content: Unorthodox.

voyage.name: The National Jewish Theatre
voyage.content: Jewish theatre located adjacent to the Nożyk Synagogue. Teatr Żydowski is the only theatre in the world that regularly performs plays in Yiddish.

voyage.name: Kinoteka
voyage.content: Comfortable cinema in the heart of the city.

voyage.name: Multikino
voyage.content: Your usual multiplex in a shopping centre, but the central location makes it very convenient to visit. There is an exquisitely appointed bar for pre- or post-show drinks. It can get obnoxiously crowded in the evenings or on the weekends.

voyage.name: Kino Luna
voyage.content: This cinema's marquee displays a wide variety of films from Polish films to Hollywood productions to other more independent and "foreign", that is to Poland, films. On Thursdays, the films are shown with English subtitles.

voyage.name: Kino Kultura
voyage.content: A place with high ambitions and lots of history to back it up, a unique location on the Royal Route and a nice cafe/restaurant with a garden. The choice of movies shown is a bit broader than everywhere else, with a high content of independent international cinema, with Polish and Central European films in particular.

voyage.name: Kino Muranów
voyage.content: Uniquely located in elegant 1950s arcades of the socrealist building ensemble, it has a special atmosphere and is known for frequent themed weeks devoted to cinematography of a particular country or genre.

voyage.name: Złote Tarasy
voyage.content: This large shopping mall sprawls over four levels and is covered by a unique glass roof. It is located right next to the Dworzec Centralny and is accessible from its underground level. It may be convenient for some last-minute shopping if you are departing Warsaw by train.

voyage.name: Arkadia
voyage.content: Arkadia has an interesting collection of shops, plus a much better selection of restaurants in its food court than Złote Tarasy. Arkadia also has several restaurants on its outside, at its main entrance.

voyage.name: Wars Sawa Junior
voyage.hours: Opening hours vary per store - every store has an independent entrance
voyage.content: The three former 1970s department stores form the so-called "Eastern Wall" (Ściana Wschodnia) of Marszałkowska Street between Aleje Jerozolimskie and Jasna Street, facing the Palace of Culture and Science. They buildings have now been broken up into separate retail spaces, housing popular local and international chain stores.

voyage.name: Green Bar
voyage.content: A vegetarian restaurant

voyage.name: VietMama
voyage.content: Vietnamese

voyage.name: BeKeF
voyage.content: Israeli cuisine

voyage.name: Silver Dragon
voyage.content: An Asian restaurant

voyage.name: Bar Gold Kim
voyage.content: A South East Asian restaurant

voyage.name: Zarin kebab
voyage.content: A Turkish restaurant

voyage.name: Prasowy
voyage.content: Prasowy is a staple milk bar, reinvented. Facing imminent closure, it was taken over a creative team who mixed together the traditional elements of the milk bar (cheap, homely cuisine and simple, simple decor) with trendy cultural and social events. A unique place, worth a visit.

voyage.name: Zapiecek
voyage.content: A chain of eateries scattered around the city, mostly in the Old and New Town, focusing on pierogi and other traditional Polish dishes, such as soups, pierogi, and pancakes. A fairly fixed menu with seasonal variations in alcohols - they tend to have seasonal selection – only mulled wine and hot beer in winter, for example. Other than that, the place is great, and in addition to the food you will certainly enjo

voyage.name: Casa Mia
voyage.content: A small, cozy pizzeria, Casa Mia is a great little restaurant to seek refuge and satisfy your hunger. Somewhat appallingly, Casa Mia doesn't serve alcoholic beverages, though they have non-alcoholic beer.

voyage.name: Chłopskie Jadło
voyage.content: A chain of restaurants from Kraków, literally: "peasant's food". Good place to taste traditional Polish fare and enjoy wooden rustic environment. Soups are served in bread, while complementary smalec (lard) is free, so that you have no choice but trying it here.

voyage.name: Piwna Kompania
voyage.content: Located on the border between the Old and New Town, this pub serves king-size portions of traditional Polish fare. Meals are accompanied by a free dish of pickled cucumbers and sauercraut, while the bill comes with a shot of Polish cherry liquor. Beer is more average and solely pilsner, but it is drinkable and quite cheap. Free Wi-Fi connection. A bit noisy, but this is how a good pub should be.

voyage.name: Socjal
voyage.content: Socjal restaurant features an enormous, continuous table that can seat dozens and is good for, you guessed it, socializing. In warmer months, this is complemented by an outdoor garden. The menu is updated everyday as it is being prepared from whatever the chefs purchase fresh in the morning, and the restaurant stays open until late in the night - or even early in the morning. The menu mostly includes pizzas, pastas a

voyage.name: AleGloria
voyage.content: Flagship outlet of the TV-famed restaurateur Magda Gessler, blending traditional Polish culinary traditions with cosmopolitan and modern inspirations. One invites guests there to impress with food, sumptuous decor and ability to foot the bill.

voyage.name: Amber Room
voyage.price: Mains 70-90 zł, tasting menu 250 zł, business lunch 80 zł
voyage.content: Hosted by the historic Sobański Palace and serving as the posh canteen for the business elite congregating at the co-located Polish Council of Business, Amber Room has become something of a paragon of haute cuisine. The location is ideal for tourists wanting to enjoy a meal in the most beautiful part of Warsaw, but frequently-organised events may get in the way, so reservations are recommended, even if to check if gu

voyage.name: Belvédére
voyage.price: Main courses: 50-90 zł, Sunday Brunch: 145 zł
voyage.content: Located in the historic palm house in the Łazienki Park, it offers a very unique ambience - and charges for that accordingly.

voyage.name: Cesarski Pałac
voyage.content: Chinese.

voyage.name: Chianti
voyage.content: Instagramey, Italian splurge restaurant with pasta and wine

voyage.name: El Popo
voyage.content: Splurge Tex-Mex location with wine.

voyage.name: Le Cedre
voyage.content: Lebanese.

voyage.name: Papaya
voyage.content: Japanese and Thai.

voyage.name: Qchnia Artystyczna
voyage.content: In the Zamek Ujazdowski castle, which also houses the Centre for Contemporary Art, this artist-themed restaurant offers a suitably contemporary take on fine dining and splendid views from the escarpment from its summer terrace.

voyage.name: Ryżowe Pole
voyage.content: Japanese, sushi.

voyage.name: Smaki Warszawy
voyage.content: Polish and International.

voyage.name: St Antonio
voyage.content: Nestled in the corner of the Saxon Garden in a historic building, St. Antonio is where one takes out-of-town relatives, who may not appreciate more modern culinary inventions. The photo gallery of celebrities of bygone decades who had frequented the restaurant complements the retro decor.

voyage.name: Tandoor Palace
voyage.content: Indian restaurant with great food, augmented by unashamedly garish and tacky decor you would expect. The location is a bit out of the way, but well worth the tram ride.

voyage.name: Cafe A. Blikle
voyage.content: The Blikle family has been running this café and confisserie for two centuries now, turning it into a nationwide business with many locations across Poland - but this is the original one. Stepping inside elicits memories of a turn-of-the-nineteenth-century café, which is more than charming in Warsaw, where a well-made coffee has been replaced by iced mochas and in-and-out coffee shops. This particulabuilding is divid

voyage.name: E. Wedel
voyage.content: The best hot chocolate in Warsaw. The interior is old style and reminds you of pre-war Warsaw. Wedel's shop with stylish sweets is adjacent to the cafe.

voyage.name: Pożegnanie z Afryką
voyage.content: This inconspicuous place with a tiny sign above the door is a true paradise for coffee-lovers. Here, you don't choose the type of coffee. You first select the type of beans, and then decide whether you want it espresso, cappuccino, or perhaps as Turkish-style coffee cooked on hot sand and flavored with cinnamon, ginger, or other spices of your choice. They also have a good selection of cakes and pastries, not to ment

voyage.name: Charlotte
voyage.content: A cafe-cum-boulangerie, it was one of the first in Warsaw to bake their own breads and pastries on premises and offer wine to accompany simple, Parisian-inspired snacks. Thanks to its popularity with the media and celebrities, as well as the prime location on the Plac Zbawiciela, it became a sustained favourite - you may find yourself unable to get a table at any given time of day. The pretentious and slow service go

voyage.name: Cafe Kulturalna
voyage.content: A really cool bar in the Palace of Culture and Science. A DJ spins the beats which is occasionally enhanced by a drummer and keyboard player. They also host live music on occasion. Kulturalna attracts the college aged intelligentsia type, but can bring in the elderly, but hip too who all end up grooving on the dance floor or chill out on chairs all night.

voyage.name: Jazz Bistro
voyage.content: Good restaurant in the city centre, near the US Embassy and comes equipped with free Wi-Fi access. The restaurants hosts live musicians several times a week. The only downside to the restaurant is a side door, which leads into an office building. Bright lights from the office building shine into the restaurant, which somewhat diminishes the atmosphere of the restaurant and its music.

voyage.name: Living Room
voyage.content: A trendy bar that serves up good food and has a wide variety of elaborately created drinks.

voyage.name: Przekąski Zakąski
voyage.content: The cult joint is in the process of moving from its erstwhile prime location in Krakowskie Przedmieście to a new one in the city centre and operates in a temporary tent smack in the middle of Warsaw, continuing to draw crowds all day and night long. The main draw are obviously reasonably-priced alcoholic drinks and many cheap bites, but the menu was expanded to include more elaborate dishes prepared by the chefs from

voyage.name: Warszawa Powiśle
voyage.content: The mother of all hipster places in Warsaw operates in the former ticket sales office of the Powiśle train station, which afforded them splendid modernist architecture and a recognizable name spelled out on the impressive neon sign above the building. The cool factor of Powiśle lies in the fact that it's essentially an outdoor bar. There are no tables inside and most people either grab up the limited number of chairs

voyage.name: Tygmont
voyage.content: Tygmont is Warsaw's best known jazz club and for good reason – the musicians it hosts are good, however, there are a few caveats. On occasion, Tygmont has a weird atmosphere and can be disappointing. There are nights when one floor will be dedicated to hip hop, which seems completely out of place, while the other is dedicated to musicians playing obscenely loud music. If the club brought the decibels down, it w

voyage.name: Emma Hostel
voyage.content: Hostel named after Emma Goldman (anarcho-feminist activist) is run by a cooperative according to ecofriendly, sustainable rules. Five dorms and several doubles on two storeys in a historic tenement house, communal bathrooms, kitchen, free fair-trade tea, coffee and breakfast. Pets welcome. Discounts apply to NGO workers, activists, students and persons aged 55+ (do not apply to persons using on-line booking portals).

voyage.name: Hostel Helvetia
voyage.content: Helvetia is a cool hostel, a stone's throw away from the University of Warsaw's main campus, Nowy Swiat, and a ten minute walk to the Old Town. The staff are pleasant and helpful and the hostel occasionally hosts vodka and beer parties for its guests. Dorm 39/55 zł (Sunday-Thursday/Friday-Saturday).

voyage.name: Hostel Smolna 30
voyage.price: From 40 zł, 10% discount for the PTSM/ IYHF card owners
voyage.content: HI Hostel.

voyage.name: Hostel Agrykola
voyage.content: HI Hostel.

voyage.name: Karolkowa Youth Hostel
voyage.content: An educational institution, mainly used by Polish pupils, students, teachers and education workers. Foreign students and teachers are also welcomed. If a room is available, they can accommodate people who are not connected with education.

voyage.name: Nathan's Villa Hostel
voyage.content: This hostel has a cable TV room, and free laundry service, however, since they do not have a dryer it may take a day or two for clothes to dry. The manager will sometimes take guests to clubs. This hostel is open all day and is located only a few blocks from the city center.

voyage.name: Oki Doki Hostel
voyage.content: From the outside this big grey, ugly building doesn't look promising, but once inside you are greeted by a friendly, chatty member of staff on the 24-hr reception. Directly opposite is the bar/café/breakfast room which serves some very cheap drinks. Each room has been individually decorated by a different artist and they are given names such as 'House of the Maiden'. Also equipped with kitchen, free Internet access,

voyage.name: ibis Budget Warszawa Centrum
voyage.content: The ibis budget is a bare minimum, every-expense-spared budget hotel chain. Don't expect the door to manned all night and if you will arrive after the check-in deadline, you better arrange to be let into your room, because ibis Budget hotels may or may not have anyone on duty to let you in after a certain time.

voyage.name: Hotel Logos
voyage.price: Rooms starting at 134 zł per night
voyage.content: A very simple hotel in Powiśle - the cheapest rooms do not even have ensuite bathrooms. That said, at their prices you will probably be able to get a nicer room in other, better-equipped hotels across Warsaw.

voyage.name: The Warsaw Hostel
voyage.content: Nice hostel, friendly staff. Self-serve coffee machine (coffee grounds provided). Very basic kitchen. Common area in back of kitchen. Can get noisy on Saturday nights.

voyage.name: Mercure Warszawa Grand
voyage.content: The Grand Hotel is a part of the Mercure chain. It's in a relatively peaceful location among government offices, but close to most areas of tourist interest.

voyage.name: Mercure Warszawa Centrum
voyage.content: It is very close to the Dworzec Centralny, separated from it only by the Złote Tarasy shopping centre, which provides for an almost entirely covered walkway between the two.

voyage.name: Hotel Metropol
voyage.price: Single: €99; Double: €119. Suites are also available
voyage.content: Don't expect much of a view, unless you consider an intersection and the Novotel a view.

voyage.name: Novotel Warsaw Centrum
voyage.content: Comfortable rooms. If you ask for room one of the higher floors, you are more than likely going have an amazing view in any direction.

voyage.name: Hotel Bristol
voyage.content: The Bristol is a Warsaw landmark in its own right, imbued in history. Heads of state, royalty and various celebrities of different eras stayed here during its many decades in operation. It is also directly on the Royal Route, a short walk from Old Town and not far from many other historic attractions.

voyage.name: Regent Warsaw Hotel
voyage.content: Outside of the city centre and on the border of the Mokotów district, it requires a bus or taxi ride to get to most attractions. The Regent nevertheless remains a firm favourite with frequent travellers due to a combination of lush comfort, large bathrooms and a location at the doorstep of the Łazienki Park.

voyage.name: InterContinental Warszawa
voyage.price: €120-180 during the week, as low as €60 if booked in advance; Apartments from €2500/month
voyage.content: The 5-star InterContinental is one of Warsaw's tallest, best designed, and most luxurious hotels. The hotel optimizes its commanding height by using wide windows to provide breathtaking panorama views of Warsaw. Be sure to stop by the fitness center for the best view. All rooms have at least 32 m2 of space, spacious bathrooms that come equipped with a bath and a separate shower, and minibars. High speed internet conn

voyage.name: Warsaw Marriott Hotel
voyage.content: If you want a room with a view, you can't go wrong here, because the building is one of the tallest in Warsaw. Depending on the location of your room, you may have a view of the Palace of Culture and Science. The Panorama cocktail bar at the top floor provides great views of the city to the patrons, accompanied by steep drink prices.

voyage.name: Polonia Palace Hotel
voyage.content: 4-star luxury hotel in the centre of Warsaw. The hotel first opened in 1913 and was the best surviving hotel in Warsaw during the Second World War, hosting the embassies of several countries including the USA, UK and the Netherlands in the difficult postwar years. Eisenhower, de Gaulle and several other notable figures have been guests. The Polonia was made a protected monument in 1965.

voyage.name: Radisson BLU Centrum Hotel
voyage.content: The hotel is in the heart of the business district and tourist quarter of the city. It is close to the Palace of Culture and Science and Warsaw Central Station. There is another Radisson BLU (Sobieski) in Warsaw, not far away but in the opposite direction.

voyage.name: Sofitel Victoria Warsaw
voyage.content: Located a short distance from Nowy Świat, the Sofitel Victoria Warsaw Hotel is the prime real estate for visitors who would like to tour the Old Town on a whim. Rooms facing Plac Piłsudskiego have a really nice view.

voyage.name: Warsaw Zoo
voyage.price: Admission: Adults 30 zł, Children 6 zł, Children under three years are free
voyage.content: A relatively small zoo, but with some interesting species, including a pack of wild and rambunctious monkeys that seem to fascinate every visitor. Other Zoo residents include lemurs, giraffes, elephants, hyraxes, lions, tigers, zebras, and jaguars that live in a glass enclosure that allows you stand only centimeters away from the beasts.

voyage.name: Saint Mary Magdalene Orthodox Church
voyage.content: One of two Orthodox churches in Warsaw.

voyage.name: 19th Century Houses
voyage.content: around pl. Weteranów 1863 r., ul. Kłopotowskiego and ul. Okrzei, in particular The Jewish Mikvah built in 1840 at ul. Kłopotowskiego 31. See also the list of all historic buildings in Praga Północ.

voyage.name: Saints Michael & Florian Cathedral
voyage.alt: Katedra św. Michała Archanioła i św. Floriana

voyage.name: Barriers of Grochów
voyage.content: Used for collecting the toll for entering the city.

voyage.name: Monument to the builders of the Brześć Road
voyage.content: Built in 1825, it was the first monument in Poland to honor anonymous workers (instead of famous national heroes).

voyage.name: Saska Kępa
voyage.content: A mostly residential neighborhood that is freckled with numerous embassies, but is unique for the cozy cafes and restaurants that line one its most well-known streets, ul. Francuska. In the evening, the neighborhood is an idyllic setting for a stroll, which can be topped off by watching the sunset over the Eastern skyline of Warsaw, dominated by the Palace of Culture and Science, while grilling or drinking by a coupl

voyage.name: Praga Museum
voyage.content: Well-designed museum showcasing the history of Praga. Lots of interesting interviews with old residents.

voyage.name: Neon Museum
voyage.content: Uniquely Warsaw collection of historic neon signs. In the 1970s, Poland made a break from the grey days of Stalinism, partially by installing neon signs that harkened back to the glory days of 1920s Warsaw. As they slowly disappear due to post-Iron-Curtain development, artists and historians have started collecting and displaying them.

voyage.name: E. Wedel Chocolate Factory Museum
voyage.content: Museum of chocolate, and the Wedel family – entrepreneurs involved in its production.

voyage.name: Olszynka Grochowska
voyage.content: The forest was an important battlefield during the November Uprising.

voyage.name: Skaryszewski Park
voyage.alt: Park Skaryszewski or Park im. Ignacego Paderewskiego
voyage.content: This park isn't as well known as some of the others, most likely since a palace is absent from it, but that said, it's nonetheless a pleasant park for a stroll or to read a book and comes complete with its own lake. Near park's main entrance, there is a memorial to the September 11th terror attacks.

voyage.name: Praski Park
voyage.content: A park that's good for a stroll. There's a large sculpture of a giraffe and a playground for children within the park's grounds. Near the entrance to the Warsaw Zoo, there are a few eateries that serve up ice cream.

voyage.name: Cinema City
voyage.content: Located in CH Promenada.

voyage.name: Kino Praha
voyage.content: Studio cinema, three rooms.

voyage.name: Stadion Narodowy
voyage.content: The impressive stadium has been built on the site of an earlier communist-era venue right in time for the Euro 2012 championships. It is a multi-level entertainment, exhibition and congress venue, with a busy schedule of events. The grounds around the stadium have been arranged to hold events as well. On the nights of major matches or concerts, traffic in the area can be severely disrupted, but on other days, you may

voyage.name: Alternative Warsaw
voyage.address: Starting Point: St Florian's Cathedral (Floriańska 3, 03-707 Warszawa)
voyage.content: A 2h walking tour through Praga where you learn about the history of Praga and Warsaw in general

voyage.name: CH Promenada
voyage.content: A multi-level shopping arcade with a mixture of chain stores and upscale outlets. The layout and architecture may be a bit perplexing, and the mall has not aged well. An Alma upscale supermarket and multiplex cinema are located within the shopping centre.

voyage.name: Warszawa Wileńska
voyage.content: A shopping mall built over a terminus for local trains heading north-eastwards of Warsaw, directly connected to the namesake metro station as well. A rather wide selection of the usual chain stores, service outlets, gastronomy and a supermarket.

voyage.name: Różyckiego Bazaar
voyage.content: The most popular bazaar in Poland during the communist era, it is now largely empty.

voyage.name: Ristorante Repubblica Italiana
voyage.content: This three-room restaurant, with each of its rooms painted and decorated to correspond with the colors of Italian flag, is one of the few Italian eateries in Warsaw that does Italian right. Each dish is delicious and beautifully prepared, and the portions leave customers feeling satisfied. When the weather is nice, the restaurant's patios are a great place to enjoy your meal while observing passersby.

voyage.name: Pyzy, flaki gorące!
voyage.content: Hip little eatery specializing in various types of pyzy, a gnocchi-like potato dumpling, served with your choice of toppings in a glass mason jar. Has a good range of drinks to wash them down with and street tables for sunny days. For something a little unusual, try the liver & berry sauce.

voyage.name: Herbaciarnia na
voyage.price: About 10 - 15 zł for a small kettle of tea
voyage.content: A cozy little place where that serves a wide variety of teas.

voyage.name: Fabryka Trzciny
voyage.content: A former marmalade factory, now a cultural center with a club, a theater, a restaurant, artist ateliers and an exhibition area.

voyage.name: Stara Praga
voyage.content: Very nice hostel, with great conditions and a very helpful staff.

voyage.name: Królikarnia
voyage.price: Free entrance, both to the park and the museum
voyage.hours: Museum is open 11:00—18:00, except for Thursdays (closes 20:00) and Mondays (closed all day)
voyage.content: The Królikarnia park is named after a pretence to being a rabbit warren for the King Augustus II in the 18th century, but in reality it served as a leisure residence and a place for meetings of the arts community. Those took place in the classicist palace, modelled after the renaissance Villa Rotonda outside Vicenza by the royal architect Domenico Merlini. The palace is situated right on the slope of the Warsaw escar

voyage.name: Szuster Palace
voyage.content: A neogothic palace, once a remote park residence, now nestled between residential buildings. A reconstructed "mauretanian house" signifies the entry to the vestigial park from Puławska street. The palace is home to a musical company and not open to visitors except concert nights.

voyage.name: St Catherine Church
voyage.content: St. Catherine's is the oldest continually existing parish within Warsaw, founded in 1238. This may be a bit misleading, as the current church building is much younger, dating in its present form from 1848, but still well-worth a visit for its elegant form, picturesque hilltop location and quite pristine condition. The churchyard contains the Monument to the Victims of Communist Terror of 1944-1956.

voyage.name: National Library of Poland
voyage.content: Not a major architectural draw or a typical tourist attraction, but a massive vault of knowledge and artistic work in print and other media. If this is of interest to you, you can easily schedule hours if not days for visiting the National Library.

voyage.name: Wilanów Palace
voyage.price: Free on Thursday, first come first serve
voyage.content: Wilanów Palace is tucked away in the romantic surroundings of the royal gardens. It's an ideal place to take a date or just to relax, but be forewarned that there are a few ponds and lakes along the walking paths that are infested with mosquitoes, so be wise and protect yourself or your date with bug repellent. The interior of the palace has been converted into an art museum.

voyage.name: Poster Museum
voyage.content: The Poster Museum is for you if you're interested in seeing cool posters by the likes of Rafał Oblinski, a Polish artisan who made a big splash around the world by making posters for the New York Opera, Cincinnati Opera, and numerous American magazines.

voyage.name: Botanical Garden
voyage.content: Actually, next to the Park of Culture, although there is another bus terminus (see above). No pets allowed.

voyage.name: Polish People's Movement History Museum
voyage.content: The building in which it is situated, called The Yellow Inn (Żółta Karczma) is probably a lot more interesting than the museum itself.

voyage.name: Cinema City
voyage.content: A decent cinema in Galeria Mokotów. The upside of the theater is that the mall's food court allows you to grub out before or after the movie.

voyage.name: Warsaw Music Society
voyage.content: Classical music.

voyage.name: Tor Stegny
voyage.content: Open when the temperature falls below 10°C.

voyage.name: Galeria Mokotów
voyage.content: A large shopping mall serving the adjacent office area and most of the South of Warsaw. The main draw is the selection of upscale and luxury brands, for some of which this is the only location in Warsaw or even Poland. Otherwise the usual chain stores with mostly fashion, a Carrefour supermarket, services like hairdresser's and dry cleaning, fitness club, a large cinema and a quite nice food court in the top floor, w

voyage.name: Sadyba Best Mall
voyage.content: By comparison to other malls in Warsaw, this one is pretty small, but it comes equipped with a cinema, food court, and interestingly enough - a bowling alley, which is a one-up on most malls in Warsaw. Its cinema is also one of only a few IMAX theaters in Poland.

voyage.name: CH Land
voyage.content: A smallish and dated shopping gallery whose main draw is being right at the entrance of Metro Służew. Mostly small, non-chain stores with a variety of merchandise, including some specialist stores not usually found elsewhere. No major supermarket on location, a Biedronka discount grocery store is nearby.

voyage.name: Dominium Pizza
voyage.content: One of a chain of pizzerias.

voyage.name: Efes
voyage.content: Great place to go for a kebab.

voyage.name: Pizzeria Segment
voyage.content: A cool little pizzeria in the Sadyba neighborhood of Mokotów. The pizza is superb and there is a number of varying pizza themes. The desserts only improve the experience. In the summer, dining upstairs is nice and the restaurant has an outdoor balcony. In the winter, it's warmer to eat downstairs than upstairs.

voyage.name: Zielnik
voyage.content: Zielnik is a really cozy restaurant where couples and close friends could go for lunch, dinner, and a cup of coffee or tea. Worth a visit, if you like to get a sense of having some alone time with a friend or date. Quite expensive.

voyage.name: Park
voyage.content: Park is like Russian roulette; you may have your head blown off, or possibly have a great time. The door is relaxed, which means a lot of fools and the fashion-challenged can usually get in. Alcohol is cheap with a shot of Wyborowa only costing 5 zł. The only real problem is likely to be a concern for women. The men who go to this club often act like they have never seen a woman before, which may be due to the alcoho

voyage.name: Sikkim
voyage.content: Cool little café, where you can stop in for a cup of tea or grab some tea leaves for home.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Express Warsaw Airport
voyage.content: You may feel smarter if you stayed at a Holiday Inn Express last night and the breakfast and WiFi are free obviously, but the hotel is a bit in the middle of nowhere next to an office park and in front of a busy turnpike leading to the airport. There is a shuttle to the airport at scheduled times. Parking costs 20 zł a night.

voyage.name: Bródnowski Cemetery
voyage.content: Established 1883

voyage.name: Warsaw Fortress
voyage.content: forts

voyage.name: Camaldolese Church
voyage.content: Established in 1639 as a monastery.

voyage.name: Rampa Theatre
voyage.content: One of the best musical theatres in Poland. The building was meant to be a metro station in the 1950s when there were plans to construct a metro line on the right bank.

voyage.name: Bielany Forest Reserve
voyage.content: Many bicycle and walking paths.

voyage.name: Galeria Młociny
voyage.hours: Mon-Sat 10:00-22:00, Sun 10:00-21:00 (individual shops may have different hours.)
voyage.content: A large shopping mall, with many stores. It is quite sprawling, so depending on which door you enter from, you might need to walk a long way just to reach your shop. Includes an extensive food court.

voyage.name: Fortifications
voyage.content: that constituted the Warsaw Fortress in the 19th century. Four of them were preserved:

voyage.name: Transatlantic Radio Exchange
voyage.content: or rather ruins thereof. The twin object in Grimeton, Sweden is still preserved.

voyage.name: Sports and Recreation Centre
voyage.content: Swimming pools at ul. Oławska 3 and ul. Brygadzistów 18, sports hall at ul. Obrońców Tobruku 40.

voyage.name: Flying School
voyage.content: Parachuting, gliding, ballooning, etc.

voyage.name: Factory
voyage.content: "Designer outlet" for high-street brands, both upscale and popular.

voyage.name: Camping WOK
voyage.content: Campsite with bar, Internet, laundry. Apr-Oct. Tent: 14 zł, car 14 zł, trailer 16-20 zł, electricity 10 zł and 14 zł/person. No credit cards. Bus 146 from Dworzec Wschodni station stop Romantyczna.
